integrated_multimodal_description:
[Shot 1] Dark fantasy cinematic martial-arts animation with painterly detail and dramatic moonlit blue lighting. Begin exactly from <Picture 1>. Preserve the same adult female swordswoman, facial identity, black hair, dark layered martial-arts costume, flowing red-orange fabric, sword, body proportions, and the same gigantic horned shadow creature. Preserve the moonlit ruined environment, cold blue palette, wet reflective ground, distant traditional architecture, drifting mist, and the established spatial relationship: the swordswoman remains in the foreground-left facing the enormous creature occupying the right side of the frame.

The swordswoman holds her low combat stance for only a brief instant as her clothing and loose fabric react naturally to the wind. She then drives forcefully forward toward the creature with a fast, grounded martial-arts step, keeping her center of gravity low and her sword under firm control. Her leading foot pushes through the wet ground, producing a small burst of water and debris while her trailing fabric stretches backward from the sudden acceleration.

Without stopping or changing direction, she converts the forward momentum into one continuous sword attack. Her torso rotates, shoulders and hips turn together, and both arms guide the sword through a broad, powerful sweeping slash. The motion must remain physically connected: forward step → body rotation → sword acceleration → full sweeping strike. Do not introduce additional spins, flips, jumps, unrelated attacks, or extra weapons.

As the sword reaches maximum speed, a concentrated blue-white energy trail forms directly along the blade path. The energy begins as a narrow luminous streak close to the sword rather than appearing independently. It rapidly expands outward as the slash continues, tracing one large curved crescent through the air. The glowing sword arc sweeps from the swordswoman across the center of the frame toward the gigantic creature, pushing mist, loose particles and surface spray outward along its path.

The creature remains visually consistent with <Picture 1>: enormous black-blue body, branching horn-like structures, rough spectral texture and glowing red facial markings. It reacts to the incoming strike by leaning and recoiling slightly backward while its upper body and surrounding dark vapor are displaced by the force of the energy wave. Do not transform the creature, change its anatomy, create additional monsters, or make it disappear.

During the final phase of the shot, progressively converge toward <Picture 2>. The swordswoman advances from the lower-left foreground into the more central-left position seen in <Picture 2>. Her torso extends into the attack, her sword reaches the exact sweeping orientation of the final frame, and her red-orange trailing fabric stretches backward with the motion. The blue-white sword energy grows into the same dominant luminous crescent shape visible in <Picture 2>, curving around the swordswoman and across the frame toward the creature. The creature, moon, architecture, ground plane and overall framing progressively match the final composition.

At the 5.00-second mark, land precisely on <Picture 2>: the swordswoman is captured at the peak of the decisive sweeping slash, positioned and oriented exactly as shown in the reference; the enormous blue-white crescent sword wave dominates the middle of the frame; the gigantic horned creature recoils behind it on the upper-right; the full moon remains visible in the upper-left background; and the dark blue ruined environment, water spray, mist, debris, lighting and composition match <Picture 2> as closely as possible.

Use one continuous shot with no cuts. The camera performs a restrained lateral tracking movement following the swordswoman from left toward center while maintaining the creature's massive scale in the background. The camera must not orbit around the characters, perform a dramatic zoom, suddenly change height, or reverse direction. Keep the movement smooth and cinematic so that the transformation from <Picture 1> to <Picture 2> is driven primarily by the swordswoman's attack rather than by camera motion.

Maintain stable character identity, stable facial structure, realistic and coherent limb anatomy, correct hand-to-sword contact, a rigid and clearly defined sword, consistent costume geometry, physically plausible foot placement, coherent body rotation, stable creature anatomy, and consistent environment geometry throughout the entire shot. Preserve the painterly dark-fantasy visual style of both reference images. Use natural directional motion blur only during the fastest sword movement and energy sweep while keeping the swordswoman's face, body silhouette, sword and creature clearly readable.

overall_soundscape:
A cold nighttime wind moves continuously through the ruined environment with faint low-frequency ambience from the gigantic creature. The swordswoman's rapid footwork produces sharp wet impacts and small water splashes, accompanied by fast cloth movement. Her sword produces a clean accelerating metallic whoosh that grows into a powerful sweeping air-cut sound as the blue-white energy arc expands, followed by one deep impact pulse and a brief restrained creature roar synchronized with the completed slash. Keep all sounds clean, spatially coherent and synchronized with the visible action, with no clipping, hiss or distortion.

integrated_multimodal_description:
[Shot 1] One continuous five-second cinematic action shot in a snowy battlefield. Begin exactly from <Picture 1>. Preserve the same adult female warrior: the same white hair, facial identity, pale skin, black combat outfit, red scarf, sword, body proportions, and overall anime-styled painterly rendering. Also preserve the same snowy ruined battlefield, heavy snow atmosphere, cold white-blue lighting, splashing snow on the ground, and the same gigantic mechanical enemy units in the background with glowing orange-red core details.

At the beginning, the swordswoman is in the same low grounded crouched pose established by <Picture 1>, with one hand near the ground and the sword extended low. Her red scarf and white hair react naturally to the wind and motion. She immediately pushes off the snowy ground with explosive force, sending snow spray and loose ice particles backward. The takeoff must feel powerful and physically coherent, with clear weight transfer from the low crouch into forward acceleration.

She then drives into one continuous attack motion: a fast forward surge transitions into an upward leap, and during the ascent she rotates her torso and shoulders into a broad, powerful sword slash. The movement must read as one connected causal chain: low crouch → explosive forward burst → rising jump → full-body sword swing. Do not introduce extra flips, extra attacks, or unrelated motion. Keep the action clean, direct, and high impact.

As the sword accelerates, a bright blue-white energy trail forms directly from the blade path. This trail rapidly expands into a large luminous curved slash arc sweeping across the frame. The energy arc should feel tightly coupled to the sword motion, not independent of it. Snow, mist, and debris are displaced by the force of the movement and by the expanding energy slash, enhancing the scale of the attack.

The mechanical enemies remain visually consistent throughout: huge dark metal bodies, heavy industrial silhouettes, snow-covered surfaces, and glowing orange-red circular core lights. They should maintain their threatening presence in the background and midground. As the attack develops, the nearest central mech reacts subtly to the force of the strike, with snow and debris erupting around it, but it must not radically transform or disappear.

During the latter portion of the shot, the swordswoman rises fully into the air and converges progressively toward the exact final composition of <Picture 2>. Her body extends into a dynamic airborne attack posture, her red scarf streams dramatically behind her, and the sword completes the sweeping motion that generates the dominant blue energy arc. The spatial relationship between the airborne warrior, the giant mech below, and the snowy ruins in the background must evolve naturally into the framing of <Picture 2>.

At the 5.00-second mark, land precisely on <Picture 2>: the swordswoman is airborne above the battlefield in a strong finishing attack pose, the large blue-white sword arc sweeps prominently across the scene, the giant mech occupies the lower portion of the frame with glowing orange-red core elements, and the snowy environment, airborne debris, scale, composition, and dramatic action framing closely match <Picture 2>.

Use one continuous shot with no cuts. The camera performs a restrained cinematic tracking movement that follows the swordswoman from her low foreground-left starting position into the elevated dynamic composition of the final frame. The camera may slightly rise and widen with the action, but it must remain smooth and controlled. Do not use chaotic shake, abrupt zooms, or excessive orbiting. The motion from <Picture 1> to <Picture 2> should be driven mainly by the character’s attack and momentum.

Maintain stable character identity, stable face, stable anatomy, clean hand structure, a rigid and clearly readable sword, consistent clothing and scarf design, coherent airborne body mechanics, natural hair and cloth secondary motion, and consistent mech and environment geometry. Keep the snowy painterly aesthetic throughout. Use natural motion blur only during the fastest portions of the leap and slash, while preserving readability of the warrior, sword, scarf, and blue energy arc.

overall_soundscape:
Cold wind across an open snowy battlefield, sharp foot push-off in snow, spraying ice and snow impacts, cloth and scarf flutter, a fast rising leap sound, and a strong clean sword whoosh that expands into a powerful energy-slash sweep. Add heavy snow/debris impact accents around the mech during the final attack moment. Keep audio stable, synchronized, and free of clipping, hiss, or distortion.

integrated_multimodal_description:
[Shot 1] One continuous five-second cinematic fantasy martial-arts shot. Begin exactly from <Picture 1>. Preserve the same adult female martial heroine established by <Picture 1> and <Picture 3>: the same face, hairstyle with twin buns, green-black outfit, translucent flowing sleeves and ribbons, thigh tattoo, long ornate staff, body proportions, and elegant yet combat-ready temperament. Also preserve the same large turquoise Chinese dragon with gold whiskers and antler-like horns, along with the high-altitude cloudscape, towering cliffs, and distant ancient pagodas in the opening frame.

At the start of the shot, the heroine is riding the flying dragon in the same composition and pose established by <Picture 1>. Her hair ribbons, sleeves, and waist ornaments flow naturally in the strong wind, while the dragon moves powerfully through the sky with a serpentine body motion. The dragon immediately surges forward and slightly downward through the clouds, creating a sense of acceleration and momentum. The heroine adjusts her balance on the dragon’s back while keeping firm control of the staff.

As the motion builds, the dragon performs a strong sweeping dive through the cloud corridor toward the battlefield below. Using this momentum, the heroine launches herself cleanly off the dragon in one fluid action. She pushes off from the dragon’s back, enters a dynamic aerial descent, and rotates her torso while bringing the staff into a ready striking position. Her movement must feel physically coherent and elegant: dragon dive → leap from the dragon → airborne descent → staff rotation into attack. Do not introduce unrelated flips, teleportation, extra weapons, or abrupt pose changes.

During the descent, the environment transitions naturally from the cloud kingdom into the battle setting of <Picture 2>. Ancient East Asian architecture, stormy dramatic skies, scattered debris, and multiple hostile enemies progressively come into view. The heroine’s trailing ribbons and sleeves create strong flowing arcs around her body, emphasizing speed and grace. Her staff should remain rigid, clearly readable, and consistently designed according to <Picture 3>.

In the latter half of the shot, she completes the aerial approach and lands into a forceful sweeping strike. She plants her footing with a wide martial stance and drives the long staff across the frame in a powerful horizontal or slightly diagonal attack. The action must feel like one continuous finishing move that converts the dragon-assisted aerial entry into a decisive battlefield strike. One enemy is lifted or knocked upward by the impact, matching the airborne opponent seen in <Picture 2>, while surrounding enemies remain active in the background.

Progressively converge toward <Picture 2> during the final phase. The heroine must settle into the same dominant combat pose and composition seen in the final frame: staff extended across the frame, legs spread in a strong grounded stance, torso turned with controlled power, ribbons and sleeves streaming outward, and one enemy figure airborne in the upper-right area. The battlefield should be crowded and energetic, with traditional buildings, debris, and combat activity in the background under a dramatic sky.

At the 5.00-second mark, land precisely on <Picture 2>: the heroine is in the exact finishing attack pose and framing of the reference, using the long staff in a wide sweeping strike, with the airborne enemy, surrounding warriors, architectural environment, dramatic clouds, motion intensity, and composition closely matching <Picture 2>.

Use one continuous shot with no cuts. The camera begins with a majestic fantasy framing on the flying dragon, then performs a smooth forward and slightly descending tracking move that follows the heroine into the battlefield. The camera may subtly widen and lower as she leaves the dragon and enters combat, but it must remain cinematic and controlled. Do not use abrupt zooms, chaotic shaking, or excessive orbiting. The transition from <Picture 1> to <Picture 2> should be driven mainly by the heroine’s movement and the dragon’s dive momentum.

Maintain stable facial identity, stable anatomy, clean hands, coherent limb motion, consistent costume details, stable staff design, natural cloth and ribbon dynamics, consistent dragon anatomy, and smooth environmental continuity. Preserve a polished fantasy illustration look with strong readability, dramatic lighting, and natural directional motion blur only during the fastest movement.

overall_soundscape:
Powerful wind rushing through the clouds, subtle dragon flight movement, fluttering cloth and ribbons, one strong leap-off accent, fast descending air movement, clean staff swing whooshes, impact debris, and a sharp combat hit synchronized with the final sweeping strike that launches the enemy upward. Keep the ambience stable and cinematic, with no clipping, hiss, or distortion.
